problem.text: Let $f: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ be a function such that for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^+$, $f(x)f(y) = f(xy) + f\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)$, where $\mathbb{R}^+$ represents the positive real numbers. Given that $f(2) = 3$, compute the last two digits of $f\left(2^{2^{2020}}\right)$.

steps.title: Where to start: find $f(1)$ with $y = 1$
steps.body: We only know $f(2)$, so we need more values. Putting $y = 1$ is a good first move: then $xy$ and $\frac{x}{y}$ are both just $x$, so the equation only involves $f(x)$ and $f(1)$. Use $x = 2$, since that is the value we know.

steps.title: Set $x = y$ to get a squaring rule
steps.body:
The input $2^{2^{2020}}$ is $2$ squared over and over, so we want a rule for $f$ of a square. Putting $x = y = t$ makes $xy = t^2$ and $\frac{x}{y} = 1$, which gives $f(t)^2 = f(t^2) + f(1)$, that is,
$$f(t^2) = f(t)^2 - 2$$

steps.title: Compute the first few values
steps.body: Start from $f(2) = 3$ and apply the rule: $f(4) = 3^2 - 2 = 7$, $f(16) = 7^2 - 2 = 47$, and $f(256) = 47^2 - 2 = 2207$. The numbers grow very fast, but we only need their last two digits.

your_turn.prompt: Why are the last two digits of $f(t)$ enough to find the last two digits of $f(t^2) = f(t)^2 - 2$?
your_turn.answer: If a number is $100q + r$, its square is $100(100q^2 + 2qr) + r^2$, so the last two digits of the square depend only on $r$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Write $f(2^{2^n})$ for the $n$-th value. Working with last two digits: $n = 2$ gives $47$, $n = 3$ gives $2207$, ending in $07$, then $07^2 - 2 = 47$ for $n = 4$, then $47^2 - 2 = 2207$ ends in $07$ again. From $n = 2$ on, even $n$ always ends in $47$ and odd $n$ in $07$. Since $2020$ is even, the last two digits of $f(2^{2^{2020}})$ are **$47$**.
